description: Anti-slop house style gate. After any Write or Edit, runs the voice linter at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/../anti-slop-brain/scripts/lint_voice.py over the file that was just written. On a house style violation it exits 2, which blocks and feeds the linter output back for self-correction. It is installed and removed with this plugin and it never writes to any global or project settings file, but it is NOT skill-gated and its effect is not confined to this project: the matcher is Write|Edit with no condition on which skill is active, so while the plugin is installed it fires on every Write and Edit in every session and every repository, including ones unrelated to this project. See SECURITY.md.

comment.what_this_is: This is the plugin-level hooks file. Claude Code reads it from the plugin root, so installing or removing the plugin installs or removes this hook. It never writes to ~/.claude/settings.json and never edits any global or project settings file. Removing the plugin removes the behaviour completely. Note the limit of that statement: it describes where the hook is registered, not where it runs. While installed it is active globally, in every project, because nothing gates it on a skill or a path.
comment.exit_codes: Exit code 2 is the only blocking code. On 2, the hook's stderr is fed back to the model as the reason and the model gets a chance to correct itself. Exit code 1 does nothing useful here: it is treated as a non-blocking error, the output goes to the transcript rather than back to the model, and execution continues, so a linter failure surfaced as 1 is silently ignored. Exit code 0 is success and the stdout is not shown to the model. The wrapper therefore translates lint_voice.py's own exit 1 (findings) into exit 2, and writes the findings to stderr. lint_voice.py's exit 2 (usage error) also becomes 2, which is correct: a misconfigured gate should be loud, not silent.
comment.what_it_does_not_do: lint_voice.py enforces house style: no U+2014, no U+2013, no spaced double hyphen, plus banned tokens from a voice file. A hit is a style violation and nothing else. It is not a slop verdict, not a quality score, and never evidence about who or what wrote the text. See references/false-positives.md and references/markers-tier2.md. This hook deliberately does not run scan_residue.py or scan_placeholders.py: those are Layer 0 scanners whose findings belong in a review report, and the slop-rewrite skill carries its own scoped hook for them.
comment.failure_behaviour: Silent no-op when the linter script is absent (the sibling brain repo is not checked out), when the tool input carried no file_path, or when the written path no longer exists. A missing gate must not block unrelated work, and a blocked write on a missing dependency would be impossible for the model to fix.
comment.environment: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is exported to hook commands as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and resolves to this plugin's root directory. The linter lives in the sibling brain repo, one level up, so the path is $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/../anti-slop-brain/scripts/lint_voice.py.

hooks.command: python3 -c "import json,os,subprocess,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); p=(d.get('tool_input') or {}).get('file_path') or ''; s=os.path.join(os.environ.get('CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT',''),'..','anti-slop-brain','scripts','lint_voice.py'); r=(subprocess.run([sys.executable,s,p],capture_output=True,text=True) if (p and os.path.isfile(p) and os.path.isfile(s)) else None); bad=bool(r) and r.returncode!=0; sys.stderr.write((r.stdout+r.stderr) if bad else ''); sys.exit(2 if bad else 0)"
